caption: The drawing shows a tall, vertical boundary marker made of grey granite, standing on a rectangular base. The marker has a column-like form with slightly beveled edges and a rounded top. Near the upper section of the marker, the inscription "AIME 1824" is engraved and visible. The entire marker and its base are rendered in varying shades of grey, suggesting depth and texture. To the left of the marker, there is a block of handwritten text in black ink that gives information about the object, reading: “PERIOD 1822 SUGAR PLANTATION MARKER OF VALCOUR AIME 1798 - 1867 GENERALLY USED ON MOST PLANTATIONS FOR MARKING BOUNDARIES. GREY GRANITE LA. STATE MUSEUM.” The background of the drawing is mainly plain and off-white, with a solid black area occupying the upper left corner in a diagonal formation. A small round blue stamp appears in the bottom right area of the drawing, overlapping slightly with the base of the marker.
title: Sugar Plantation Marker
